Each mutant that survived its filtered run at base was run again at base against every bridge test (the whole_set run, with no filter and nextest's --no-fail-fast, the approval stand-in example built) before it was called a survivor, and that run was made after the tests of this change were written: the hand run, the tool run and the filtered runs came first, the tests were then written to kill what survived, and the whole_set run was then made with those tests taken out again (the tree was exactly base_commit, checked with git status and cmp). 149 of the 177 hand-written survivors and all 13 tool survivors were run that way; the other 28 had been run against every bridge test with this change's first 51 tests present (5213 tests), which survived a superset of the tests of base and so survive base too. Three of the 149 (V434, V481 and V1059) failed in the whole_set run at base, each in tests of other modules that cannot reach this file: V434 in one approved_import test_seam test (a_post_is_approved_only_by_the_token_for_its_nonce), V481 in three financial_mode_tests of tally::runtime (a_draining_refusal_after_part_of_the_standard_read_was_sent_is_not_waited_out, an_export_whose_mailing_answer_broke_off_continues_without_the_details and an_export_whose_mailing_answer_tally_declared_too_large_is_read_again_without_the_details) and V1059 in three test_seam tests (a_post_is_approved_only_by_the_token_for_its_nonce, each_dialog_child_is_told_the_voucher_count and each_dialog_is_started_in_its_own_mode). Those tests were run alone three times under each of the three mutants and three times at base (the six tests together): every one of those runs (nine under the mutants and three at base) passed all its tests (these runs, too, fell in the sleep window described next, and the three alone runs of the financial_mode test under V434 were made again afterwards). The whole_set run was then repeated once under each mutant, and those repeats ran while the host was going in and out of sleep (the power log shows repeated Sleep and DarkWake from 23:42Z to 01:59Z, and the repeats, which ran from 00:06Z to 01:34Z, were not run under caffeinate): V481 and V1059 survived all 5162 tests, taking 1149 s and 826 s, and V434 failed one test, a different one (a_draining_refusal_after_part_of_the_standard_read_was_sent_is_not_waited_out of tally::runtime, which had passed 3 of 3 alone under V434), which is not evidence either way. So V434's whole_set run was made once more at 04:08Z, under caffeinate and with no sleep in the power log during it, at base (the whole bridge lib with the 54 tests of this change excluded by the filter, not removed: 5162 ran and passed, 62 skipped, which are the 8 of base and the 54), after its financial_mode test had passed 3 of 3 alone under V434 again; a first attempt of that run, made without the build settings of the other runs (the example stand-in was missing from its target folder, so ten approved_import dialog tests failed for that reason, as a failure of the run and not of the mutant), was discarded and made again as described. So no test fails under any of the three mutants consistently. Those failures were flakes, not kills: V434, V481 and V1059 count as survivors of the whole_set run, as the rest do, and the record credits no flaky test as a killer. The same two modules had failed flakily in earlier runs: the baseline whole run with this change's first 51 tests present failed once, in each_dialog_is_started_in_its_own_mode, which then passed 3 of 3 alone at base and never failed in the 28 runs that followed. Every survivor left at this_commit is listed in accepted_survivors with its reason: an equivalent one is marked equivalent, and one that is neither killed nor equivalent starts "not killed, and not equivalent:" and is counted under accepted_not_equivalent. A hand-written mutant's mutation id is the first 32 hex digits of the SHA-256 of its edits in order, each as its from text, a NUL byte, its to text and a NUL byte, in UTF-8. Each edit's from text occurs exactly once in the file at base_commit, and applied_to names the file it was applied to. A tool mutant is named as cargo-mutants --list names it, by line and column. A mutant whose edit does not compile is recorded as unviable with the compiler's reason, not as caught. The survivors_again run was made against the 90 tests of the two test modules (agent::agent_import::verification::unmatched_cause_tests:: and agent::agent_import::tests::number_identity_tests::), the 36 that exist at base and the 54 this change adds, a subset of the tool and hand runs' filter in which every test this change adds lives and the only modules whose tests the change alters; the other tests of the filter are as at base, so a mutant that survived the filter at base cannot be killed by them now. Every mutant that survived the whole_set run was run against all 90 of them after the last test was added, so a mutant killed there is killed by them, and every mutant that remains (each entry of accepted_survivors) was run against all of them. Every run was made on macOS with CARGO_INCREMENTAL=1 and CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0 (the object files and incremental cache of the target folder were cleared during the runs to keep each build from slowing). The file has no platform-specific code (its only cfgs are cfg(test) on two functions that exist for the tests, and the path attribute of the test module), so a macOS run measures every mutant in it on the code that Windows and Linux compile; the one width-dependent mutant, V501 (u64::try_from(sent) failing, which needs a usize wider than 64 bits), is recorded not killed, and not equivalent.
